reviewer: research-data author; not an independent review of own generated material
review_order: Viewed a sheet concealing label, source ID, acceptance stratum, and gate reason; recorded observable scene/pose concerns, then read the separate ledger. Visual disease cues can remain apparent.

findings.blinded_observation: The subject is very small initially and grows substantially in the image; the first still lacks a usable pose. This is strong scale and observation-availability variation.
The walking subject is visible beside a parked vehicle, but raw pose output is absent in the middle still and limited in the others.
A crowded scene contains several walking people, and raw detections appear to select different foreground people across the sampled stills.
Two people overlap in a supported-walking scene. The raw pose points predominantly follow the assisting person rather than the supported walker.
A distant hallway subject is visible, but raw pose points disappear in the middle and final stills; the last still includes a fade/darkened image.
The same apparent walker approaches the camera. Initial raw support is absent and the final upper body is cropped at the image edge.
A single apparent walker with support devices remains visible across the sampled stills; pose points are generally on the same person.
Other people are present, and a passing cyclist partially occludes the walking subject in the last sampled still. Pose support does not prove unoccluded anatomy.
Split-screen before/after footage contains two displayed movement sequences. Raw output is absent in distant frames and follows one displayed person later; the single-person assumption is weak.
A stooped walking subject is visible across the sampled stills; some upper-body anatomy lies outside the image while the distal legs remain visible.

conclusion: The sampled rejected strata expose observation, crowding, and identity-selection failures that the box/support gates detect. Accepted sequences still contain scale variation, frame-edge cropping, and occlusion, so gate passage does not establish full tracking or anatomical validity.
limits: Only first/middle/last sampled frames of ten sequences were inspected.
No clinical diagnosis, identity continuity across every frame, or unseen sequence validity was assessed.
This qualitative check is descriptive and does not independently validate the complete dataset.
